beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Museum of Good Reasons explores a fictional institution built around justification.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its exhibits explain how things disappear without anyone admitting theft.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Mara arrives to catalogue objects inside this unsettling museum.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Behind their official descriptions are people whose losses resist tidy explanations.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel turns that distance into a mystery of work and attention.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its appeal lies in following what a persuasive account leaves out.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An ordinary lamp becomes the entrance to a much larger unease.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The museum's facade imitates windows without allowing anyone to see through them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its light is measured because daylight would change without authorization.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Mara enters an institution whose arrangements already express a theory of fairness.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The opening makes that theory strange before presenting it as an argument.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Objects, forms, and small rules give the place its distinctive atmosphere.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Even entering requires a visitor to accept rules about describing harm.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The details make the institution persuasive as well as disturbing.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An umbrella arrives with a file much larger than the object.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Mara must connect its official history to what remains in front of her.
